title: 3rd Stopping Place 2nd Truth In Sum The Indication Of Mercifulness To Unity And Oneness

questions.question: What two ideas does the passage say mercy shows at the same time?
questions.answer: It shows Allah’s unity and His oneness within that unity.

questions.question: Which living beings are given special attention in the passage when mercy is described?
questions.answer: All living creatures are included, especially those that have just come into the world.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the way needs are provided?
questions.answer: It says their needs are delivered in a very orderly and careful way, with nothing left out.

questions.question: What does the passage say mercy does not do when caring for creatures?
questions.answer: It does not overlook any of their needs.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying mercy reaches individuals everywhere at the same moment?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s care is not limited to one place or one group, but extends to all at once.

questions.question: Why does this all-reaching care point to unity?
questions.answer: Because one perfectly ordered care covers everything, which shows one source is managing it.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the truth of Opening and the truth of Mercifulness?
questions.answer: Both are said to prove unity clearly; one does so through forming beings in order, and the other through caring for living things in order.

questions.question: What part of life in this world is highlighted as evidence of mercy?
questions.answer: The arrival of living beings into worldly life and the way they are provided for.

questions.question: What happened after the traveler saw this sign?
questions.answer: He recognized another truth called the Third Truth in the Third Stopping-Place.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the marked passage?
questions.answer: It explains how divine mercy caring for all living things points to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what feature of all beings formed through Opening makes the proof very clear?
questions.answer: Their forms are made and spread out with regularity and order.

questions.question: In the passage, what quality of mercy makes it broad and far-reaching?
questions.answer: It includes everything and reaches all creatures.

questions.question: What kind of creatures are mentioned as entering the life of this world?
questions.answer: Animate beings, meaning living creatures.

questions.question: Which group among these living creatures is especially mentioned?
questions.answer: Those newly brought into life.

questions.question: What three qualities describe how they are cared for?
questions.answer: They are cared for with order, regularity, and complete provision.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the statement that none of their needs are forgotten?
questions.answer: The care is full, aware, and exact, not careless or partial.

questions.question: How does the passage connect care for individuals with care for all?
questions.answer: It says each individual is reached, and this happens everywhere at the same time.

questions.question: Why does simultaneous care support the idea of oneness within unity?
questions.answer: Because many separate creatures are cared for through one all-encompassing mercy.

questions.question: What transition happens at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The traveler moves from this truth to witnessing a third truth at another stopping-place.

questions.question: What truth in the passage is said to embrace all things?
questions.answer: The truth of Mercifulness.

questions.question: What result comes from the ordered making of the forms of beings?
questions.answer: It gives a very obvious proof of unity.

questions.question: What action of mercy is emphasized toward living creatures?
questions.answer: Mercy raises and supports them when they come into worldly life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the delivery of necessities?
questions.answer: It says necessities reach living beings in an organized and dependable way.

questions.question: How complete is this provision according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is complete enough that nothing needed is neglected.

questions.question: What does “everywhere at the same instant” help the reader understand?
questions.answer: That this mercy is universal and not limited by place.

questions.question: Who is said to witness the next truth after this reflection?
questions.answer: The traveler is the one who witnesses it.

questions.question: What is one clear sign in the passage that mercy is not random?
questions.answer: It works with consistent order and regularity.

questions.question: Who receives this mercy according to the passage?
questions.answer: All living beings that enter the world receive it.

questions.question: What special example is singled out among those living beings?
questions.answer: Those that have just begun life are singled out.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to the needs of these creatures?
questions.answer: Their needs are brought to them.

questions.question: What does it mean that none of them are forgotten?
questions.answer: It means every creature’s needed provision is included in this care.

questions.question: How wide is the reach of this mercy?
questions.answer: It reaches all individuals in every place.

questions.question: What time-related detail makes the argument even stronger?
questions.answer: The passage says this mercy reaches all of them at the same time.

questions.question: What truth is compared with Mercifulness at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is compared with the truth of Opening.

questions.question: In what way are these two truths alike?
questions.answer: Both serve as strong evidence for divine unity.

questions.question: What does the ending of the passage prepare the reader for?
questions.answer: It prepares the reader to move on to the Third Truth.

questions.question: What does the passage use as evidence that there is one ruler over creation?
questions.answer: It uses the universal and orderly care shown through mercy.

questions.question: Why is the care of newly living creatures especially meaningful?
questions.answer: Because they are in special need and yet are still provided for carefully.

questions.question: What does the passage say about mistakes or missing needs in this care?
questions.answer: It presents the care as complete, with nothing left out.

questions.question: How does the passage connect order with belief?
questions.answer: It treats order as a sign that the world is under wise and single control.

questions.question: What lesson can be drawn from mercy reaching individuals in all places?
questions.answer: Allah’s care is not local or limited; it covers all creation.

questions.question: What is proven by the truth of Opening, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The ordered forming and unfolding of beings proves unity very clearly.

questions.question: What is proven by the truth of Mercifulness, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The ordered care of living beings proves both unity and oneness within unity.

questions.question: What does the traveler’s next step show about the structure of the discussion?
questions.answer: It shows the argument moves from one sign of faith to another in stages.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes the proof from Opening almost impossible to deny?
questions.answer: The clear order and regular pattern in how beings are formed and unfolded.

questions.question: What does the passage say mercy includes?
questions.answer: It includes all things.

questions.question: When does mercy especially appear in the lives of animate beings in this passage?
questions.answer: It appears as they come into existence and enter life in this world.

questions.question: Which subgroup of animate beings is especially pointed out?
questions.answer: Those newly entering life.

questions.question: What two words describe the manner of this nurturing?
questions.answer: It is described as orderly and regular.

questions.question: What is the role of necessities in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: The fact that necessities arrive properly shows deliberate and caring provision.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by saying no need is left out?
questions.answer: It teaches that divine care is exact and all-aware.

questions.question: How does mercy reaching everyone everywhere strengthen the message?
questions.answer: It shows the care is universal and comes from one source over all.

questions.question: How does mercy reaching all at the same instant deepen that message?
questions.answer: It shows that this one source is fully powerful and directly active with every creature.

questions.question: What does the traveler witness after understanding this truth?
questions.answer: He witnesses the Third Truth in the Third Stopping-Place.
